feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is clearly aligned, the progression is logical, and the scope feels substantial. It reads professionally and is rich in relevant detail, though it would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and less repetition across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a senior digital/platform leadership profile in mission-driven organizations.  
- Strong credibility: large-scale website migration, analytics stack expansion, studio buildout, and AI search work create clear evidence of breadth and seniority.  
- Writing quality is generally polished and concise, with no obvious misspellings; terminology is modern, relevant, and appropriate for digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scope: e.g., engagement lifts, efficiency gains, search improvements, campaign performance, cost savings, or adoption results.  
- Reduce duplication between Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidating these would improve scannability and shorten the CV.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should drop the comma; “scripting, and production” should drop the comma; date style varies (“Oct.”/“Sept.”), and “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization may look inconsistent unless intentional.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads broad and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and slightly tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems, governance models and content operations. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial workflows, multimedia programs and AI-enabled discovery experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with “modernizing” or “leading” for a more senior, executive tone.
- Add a scale cue if space allows, e.g., “10,000+ page websites,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Keep “AI-enabled” and “public-sector” because they differentiate the profile and align with recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are repeated in Core Competencies; keep the intro higher-level.
- “Enterprise web modernization” overlaps with the subtitle; avoid mirroring the same phrasing exactly.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership”
- Replace generic terms with sharper, broader ones: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences”; “Automation and platform integration” instead of “workflow automation and platform integration”
- Prioritize most strategic strengths first; move “Multimedia production and livestream operations” later as a supporting competency
- Consider revised full list: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several phrases already used in the header, especially “enterprise web modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled” language
- Overlaps strongly with Topline Skills; this section should stay broader and less tool-specific
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats several points already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it more scannable and additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as a concise 1-line case study.
- Tighten wording: “AI-enabled” appears repeatedly; vary phrasing and reduce stacked nouns.
- Emphasize what was distinctive: platform, audience use case, or deliverable type (e.g., Drupal 10 microsite, interactive conference display, recurring video program).
- If possible, add 1 measurable result or scope point to 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with NACo bullets; reframe these as selected examples rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all entries; vary verbs for stronger rhythm.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic outcomes, and only the newest/highest-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web governance, campaign infrastructure, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate execution bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g., “Built Drupal campaign experiences and reusable content modules to support member storytelling, downloadable toolkits, and scalable microsite launches.”
- Reframe technical work at a higher level: replace “Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting” with “Led platform enhancements, CMS implementation, and issue resolution for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add outcomes where possible: number of microsites/toolkits launched, workflow time saved, search relevance gains, adoption by teams, or performance improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance… across web, email, social and multimedia” repeat themes already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role.
- The AI search and microsite details also duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level if those projects remain below.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the biggest transformation: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused; add metrics if available (open rates, follower growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings): “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials…”
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s analytics and publishing infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-programming language may duplicate the older advocacy video bullets unless framed here as studio-building and scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct achievement-based position. Tighten it around what changed under your leadership and add any measurable growth if available.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Replace “helping” phrasing with direct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this role more execution/scale-focused, not enterprise leadership-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as expansion/operationalization rather than initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with more distinctive, senior-level language tied to recent roles.
- Emphasize governance, enterprise modernization, and cross-channel operations over generic “content planning.”
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & publishing systems
- Cross-channel communications operations
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim; consider varying wording to avoid echo.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize current strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” is stronger than listing multiple CMSs first.
- Prioritize recent/high-value skills; move older or secondary platforms later.
- Tighten wording and group related items for readability.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences • WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation”; keep this section higher-level, not exhaustive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize business impact and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than a software inventory.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI design and dashboarding • Executive reporting and decision support • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to outcomes from the 2022–2024 role, such as supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating every tool here if the full stack is already listed in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit
- Replace with more senior, outcomes-oriented phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the studio build and leadership level in recent roles.
- Use “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” instead of separate “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” for concision.
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale/context tied to recent work (e.g., “built first in-house studio”) in experience bullets, not here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in Director/Associate roles, so this skills line should stay concise and non-repetitive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to another section or drop it if usage was light.
- Add a light qualifier to show depth, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages**.
- If formatting allows, rename to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner alignment with the rest of the CV.
- Keep it concise; avoid listing tools here that are better covered under coding/technical implementation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one more specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modernize older terms where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • API and third-party integrations • Google Tag Manager implementation • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD and deployment automation (GitHub Actions)**
- Consider grouping by function rather than listing tools randomly; this makes the section feel more senior and intentional.
- If accurate, replace broad terms with stronger specifics: e.g., **REST APIs**, **custom GTM event tracking**, **build/deployment workflows**, or **performance/security scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears in Topline Skills; keep the fuller detail here and shorten/remove it there.
- **API integrations** and workflow/automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more strategic by separating automation tools from collaboration platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance to recent work and leadership value: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central to measurable improvements, reference outcomes in recent roles instead of here (e.g., workflow standardization, cross-team coordination, reduced manual steps).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are generic unless tied to operational impact elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, frame these as platforms used for member communications and engagement workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize phrasing: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add light context for impact: **Enterprise/member email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, consider ordering by recency/strength of use rather than brand recognition.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat audience-size claims here unless you add distinct capability language.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused rather than strategic.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In a technical section, it should emphasize methods and implementation depth, not repeat broad concepts.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation”
- Replace weaker nouns like “Dashboarding” with higher-value capability language such as “KPI design” or “reporting architecture.”
- Consider swapping “A/B testing” for “Experimentation” only if you’ve directly run tests; otherwise remove it to avoid overstating hands-on optimization work.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item closely repeats Topline Skills [3]; differentiate by making this list tool/method-specific and leaving broader analytics leadership language in Topline Skills.
- “SEO” also overlaps with “SEO and performance analysis” above; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs or scale you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience reach, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, specify tools/platforms or ownership level (e.g., managed publishing calendar, led livestream production, trained junior staff).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or piloting the format here.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced member engagement.
- Consider a stronger action/result version: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, establishing an early multimedia channel for member and policy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support + first podcast.
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia work already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Since this is a tools list, keep it software-focused and avoid repeating capabilities already demonstrated in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to named tools plus one concise production qualifier: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows”
- Consider replacing “Podcast production” with a tool/platform if relevant (e.g., Riverside, Descript, OBS, vMix, StreamYard); otherwise it reads like a responsibility, not a technical skill.
- If these tools are current strengths, order by strongest/recentest use: Premiere Pro • Audition • livestream workflows • Photoshop • Illustrator.
